subject: Using student t distribution for random effects?

messages.author: 25ce5e85187da1a3
messages.subject: Using student t distribution for random effects?
parts:
Dear INLA experts,

I want to use INLA to fit random effects meta-analysis models. I can fit a Normal-Normal hierarchical model with INLA (observations are normally distributed and latent variable is normally distributed). But, I also want to fit a Normal-Student t hierarchical model as suggested here http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/17477434.

I dont know whether it is very simple question but is it possible to use INLA for such models, or it is not possible because it is not Latent Gaussian Model anymore?

Thank you very much for your help,

Best,

Burak

Exactly, that is what I was looking for, thank you very much.

In paper you wrote, "There is also a plan to extend the R package INLA to include options that allow the user to add flexibility and challenge the Gaussian assumptions of some components of the latent field in a straightforward and intuitive way."

Is this feature already implemented to R-INLA? Otherwise, is the R-code for example of Section 4.2 available from somewhere? (like the R-code of Section 4.1 which is in the appendix)

Thanks and best,

Burak

partly. we did this years ago, following an 'importance sample
approach':


@Article{art531,
> author = {T. G. Martins and H. Rue},
> title = {Extending {INLA} to a class of near-{G}aussian
> latent models},
> journal = {Scandinavian Journal of Statistics},
> keywords = {year2014,my.own,my.cv},
> year = 2014,
> volume = 41,
> number = 4,
> pages = {893--912}
> }
> n their appendices (example 4.1).



but it was never followed up.

these non log-concave distributions are really annoying.... ;-)

H
